B.explanation: Volume decreases by $0.0040 \text{ m}^3$, so final volume is $0.012 - 0.0040 = 0.0080 \text{ m}^3$.

hints: Notice the phrase work is done on the gas at constant pressure of $1.0 \times 10^5 \text{ Pa}$ starting from $0.012 \text{ m}^3$ - work on the gas means it is compressed.
Recall that for constant pressure, the work linked to volume change is $W = p\Delta V$, so you can find $\Delta V$ from $400 \text{ J}$ and $1.0 \times 10^5 \text{ Pa}$.
Calculate $\Delta V$ in $\text{m}^3$ and then subtract it from the initial $0.012 \text{ m}^3$ to get the smaller final volume.
walkthrough: Identify the process: initial volume $V_1 = 0.012 \text{ m}^3$, constant pressure $p = 1.0 \times 10^5 \text{ Pa}$, and $400 \text{ J}$ of work done on the gas, so the gas is compressed.
State the rule for constant-pressure work: magnitude $W = p \Delta V$, where $\Delta V$ is the magnitude of the volume change.
Rearrange and substitute: $\Delta V = W/p = 400 / (1.0 \times 10^5) = 0.0040 \text{ m}^3$. Units check: $\text{J Pa}^{-1} = \text{m}^3$.
Apply compression: final volume $V_2 = V_1 - \Delta V = 0.012 - 0.0040 = 0.0080 \text{ m}^3$.
